summary: Antonio Terrone is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Leiden University by 2010, supervised by Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and has served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Antonio Vigilante works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Bari (2009–2012) and has held teaching posts at Liceo Piccolomini (2015) and the University of Siena (2025–2026), alongside directing Educazione Aperta (2023).
Antonín Jan Jungmann (1775–1854) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Charles University (Dr.med. 1800–1805), where he subsequently served as Professor of Medicine from 1808 to 1850.

Anuj Misra is a scholar of Indology and history. After completing an MSc at the University of Cape Town and a PhD at the University of Canterbury under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, he became a professor at the Free University of Berlin in 2024.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee (1911–1999) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta, where he taught Pali, and later served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981–1982).

Anupam Chakraborty works in Indology and other fields. He earned a Bachelor of Business Administration from Bengal School of Technology and Management (2019–2022) and completed an MBA at the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur (2023–2025).
Anuradha Seneviratna (1938–2009) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya (~1961–1965) and later served there as a professor from ~1984 to 2004.

Anushka Kahandagamage is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned an MA at the University of Colombo, an MPhil at South Asian University, and a PhD at the University of Otago, before holding a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard University (2025–2026).
Anvita Abbi (b. 1949) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Cornell University (~1971–1975) and served on an editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1976–2013).
Aparajita Kundu is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. She completed a PhD at Jadavpur University and serves as an Assistant Professor at Surendranath College.

Aram Frenkian (1898–1964) specialized in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University and the University of Bucharest (PhD 1931), later serving as Professor of Greek at Chernivtsi University (~1937–1945) and the University of Bucharest (1945).

Archibald Campbell (1805–1874) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the universities of Glasgow, Edinburgh (Dr.med. ~1823–1827), and Cambridge (M.A.), where he later lectured in Indian Law at the university and Pembroke College.

Archibald Campbell Carlleyle (1831–1897) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an assistant to Cunningham at the Archaeological Survey of India (1871–1885) and as curator at the Riddell Museum (~1871–1885).

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned an M.A. at Oxford, studying under Monier Monier-Williams, and held posts including Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Benares Sanskrit College and Principal and Professor of Philosophy at the University of Allahabad.

Archie John Bahm (1907–1996) specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Albion College and the University of Michigan, he held faculty posts at Texas Tech University, the University of Denver, and the University of New Mexico (1948–1973).

Arend Willem Mauritz Odé (1887–1951) was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. from Leiden University, studying under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and also studied at the University of Copenhagen under Holger Pedersen. He served as a teacher and conrector at Grotius College.
Arghyadip Mondal is a researcher in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. He is affiliated with Ghent University as a PhD researcher (attested 2026).

Ariana Maki is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at Ohio State University (2012) and held positions at the University of Colorado Boulder, the University of Idaho, and the University of Virginia.

Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. Succeeding Marcelle Lalou, she held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972) and taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.
Arild Engelsen Ruud is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a PhD at the London School of Economics (1991–1995) and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 2007.
